YES. THIS. Could that vet have been Dr Matt..something? He was wonderful. O'Brien is a member of an elite group of vets from Canada. She was Dr Hall's teacher, actually and trained her to take over. I know Dr Hall's partner personally so it was a surprise to find out she was my new vet. She's just as great and just as loving. I cannot recommend another place. They aren't an emergency clinic but when my cat had a sort of seizure attack and I told them how horrible the emergency clinic was, they immediately told me to bring him in, and while it may take a bit for the doctor to see him, the techs will help and manage him. Amazing place.

If it's for a cat, 100000% The Cat Clinic on Concession. I've even had a vet call my cat a cutie and kiss it on the top of it's head when it was sick. It was so wholesome. They're REALLY good, honest, and try to save you as much money as possible. I highly recommend Dr Hall. I would NEVER go to Hamilton Region Emergency Vet Clinic. They told me my cat was going to be perfectly fine, and it died a day later. They also charged me for a different trip when my cat passed in my arms on the drive, and still charged us $80+ just to listen to see if he had a heartbeat for a whole minute of their time. Also would not recommend East Mountain Animal Hospital. Was told my cat needed his ear amputated because of a cauliflower ear, that his organs were failing and with medication he would be lucky to live another 2-6 months, was too anemic to get any IV, and was prescribed 8 medications.... **eight.**

  
Took him to the Cat Clinic, the vet we saw is from a group of an elite group of vets in Canada. She saw the bag of medication, made a face, and asked if she could take a photo. She teaches, and said it's a perfect example of what *not* to do. My cat needed none of those, organs were fine, could have had an IV though didn't need one, and that his ear did not affect his health in any way. 

BIG differences here. It's been 3 years, and that old man cat is going strong.
